rubrics.criterion: The per-batch training step again delegates target construction and sampling instead of embedding them: RPN regression/label targets and ROI classifier targets come from well-scoped target-assignment/sampling units, with the IoU overlap, threshold labelling, matching fix-up, subsampling and bboxes-to-deltas arithmetic no longer re-derived inside the step (including the duplicated second copy under per-site name prefixes).
rubrics.rationale: The training step is the deepest absorption in this instance - a creator->assignment->matching/encode chain collapsed into the step body with two adapted copies of the same math - so its restoration is the core of the requested repair.

rubrics.criterion: The proposal path delegates again: the network forward obtains the anchor tensor and per-image proposals from the units that own those responsibilities, so grid enumeration and the decode/clamp/filter/sort/NMS/pad pipeline (with its per-image locals and hoisted component aliases) no longer live in the forward body or its loop.
rubrics.rationale: The proposal forward is the second multi-level absorption site and the only one nested inside a per-image loop; leaving it embedded would leave a profiler-critical path structurally untouched.

rubrics.criterion: The evaluation callback and the dataset item accessor delegate again: per-image sizing/conversion/resize/normalization, box decoding and coordinate correction are obtained from the shared helpers/decode unit rather than embedded in the callback, and per-sample loading/augmentation/letterboxing is obtained from the class's shared data method rather than embedded in the accessor (its duplicated per-branch assembly tail included).
rubrics.rationale: These two sites are the per-iteration faces of evaluation and training; they absorb shared preprocessing and decode responsibilities that other entry points still use through the untouched units.

rubrics.criterion: Restored delegation keeps every existing consumer working: the prediction entry point, the evaluation/mAP flow and the collate function all still operate through the same units with unchanged meaning and contract (constructor arguments and forward signatures, dataset item shape CHW-float-image plus boxes plus labels, detection-results txt format).
rubrics.rationale: The absorbed units are shared by callers the repair must not break; this task's risk is exactly that a re-extraction forks or strands a caller of the shared preprocessing, decode or sampling units.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not leave competing copies of the same responsibility behind: no near-duplicate of a shared helper (or stripped private variant of it) is left next to the original for one call site, and no absorbed fragment survives relocated-but-still-inlined inside the repaired method.
rubrics.rationale: The injected state second-sources the same knowledge under per-site names; a cosmetic extraction that keeps second copies would recreate the maintenance hazard the task describes.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not change the meaning of the shared units' parameters or thresholds for the sake of the extraction (IoU/positive/negative thresholds, sample counts and ratios, min-size scaling, pre/post-NMS counts, encode/decode epsilons and normalization std all keep their values and call sites).
rubrics.rationale: Extraction is tempting to 'clean up' by unifying constants that were deliberately shared; any value-level unification is a behavior change in this instance, not a repair.

rubrics.criterion: No debris from the embedded fragments remains: module-level imports that were added solely to serve the inlined copies are removed if unused, and locals/aliases that existed only to feed the copied bodies (per-image *_t names, hoisted component aliases, fragment-specific constants bound at method entry) are not left as dead bindings.
rubrics.rationale: The injection added two imports and a set of hoisted aliases specifically for the embedded copies; leaving them behind is a concrete, checkable residue of this instance.

rubrics.criterion: Comment blocks rewritten for the embedded layout (the hot-path/avoid-call-overhead justifications and the recomputed step descriptions inside the four methods) do not survive as misleading standalone narration of logic that now lives in the delegated units.
rubrics.rationale: The injected comments describe inline computation as if it belonged in the caller; keeping them unchanged misdocuments the restored delegation and confuses the next reader.

rubrics.criterion: The order and count of every random draw are preserved relative to the injected state: numpy subsampling draws during RPN/ROI target assignment and sampling, the proposal-padding choice draw, and the dataset augmentation draws occur in the same sequence, so any fixed seed reproduces the same losses, proposals, detections and items.
rubrics.rationale: This task re-plumbs order-sensitive sampling paths; a repair that reorders, batches or re-seeds draws (e.g. by moving np.random calls into or out of loops, or fusing two draws) changes seeded results, which the prompt forbids.

rubrics.criterion: End-to-end behavior is unchanged: with identical inputs and seeds, the computed losses, proposal tensors, detection-results txt bytes and dataset items (image tensor content, boxes, labels, including the grayscale-input conversion branch and empty-ground-truth handling) are identical before and after the repair.
rubrics.rationale: The absorbed fragments also carry guards and branches (grayscale conversion, empty-source decode, empty-ground-truth assignment) whose loss or drift would silently corrupt evaluation and training on edge-case inputs.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not alter the pipeline's observable outputs as a side effect of extraction (no changes to background class offset or label sign conventions, classifier-score axis ordering, box corner conventions, letterbox fill color, resize filter, coordinate normalization between network and pixel spaces).
rubrics.rationale: Plausible, tempting side effects specific to this injection: the embedded decode and correction fragments make it easy to silently flip conventions between the training, proposal, eval and data paths while 'extracting'.

rubrics.criterion: The repository's complete test suite passes on the repaired tree.
rubrics.rationale: The suite pins the geometry, encoding/decoding, scheduling, callback, loader and collate behavior of this project; it is the executable definition of 'no behavior change' for this instance.
